issues.description: The template Lecture class declares addGuestStudents with two parameters (int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput), but the problem statement UML and the solution implement addGuestStudents(int) with a single int parameter. This mismatch in method signature is structural and will confuse students about the correct method to implement and use (and may cause compilation/test failures if they follow the template signature).
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the specification and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* TODO: implement */ }. Remove the extra boolean parameter from the template method and update any related TODO/comments to reflect the expected single-parameter behavior.

issues.description: The method addGuestStudents is specified in the problem statement as addGuestStudents(int) and implemented in the solution with a single int parameter, but the template declares addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput). This signature mismatch (extra boolean parameter in the template) creates a naming/usage inconsistency that will confuse students trying to map the task description to the starter code and the expected solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template method signature match the problem statement and solution by changing the template stub to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* ... */ } (or, if input validation is required, update the problem statement and solution to include and document the boolean parameter).
